reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch G3-MG-Harden (mat_g3_mg_q1_2..mat_g3_mg_q1_6), 2026-08-17

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The generator successfully meets the core competency by testing the student's ability to identify points, lines, line segments, and rays, using definitional properties, visual models, and drawing procedures. Questions such as 'Look at the model: • P (a single dot with a label). Which geometric figure is represented?' and 'When drawing a line, what symbols are placed at both ends to show it extends forever in both directions?' fulfill the requirements.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All parts of the competency are covered: points ('Look at the model: • P (a single dot with a label).'), lines ('When drawing a line, what symbols are placed at both ends'), line segments ('To draw a line segment measuring 4 cm'), and rays ('When drawing a ray, what symbol is placed at one end'). Both recognizing using models ('A beam of light starting from a flashlight and travelling outward in one direction is a real-world model of a ___.') and the concept of drawing are evaluated.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The language and conceptual difficulty are fully appropriate for Grade 3. The use of simple, familiar models like 'A beam of light starting from a flashlight' and drawing instructions like 'you start at the 0 cm mark on a ruler and draw until which mark?' match the developmental capacity of a 3rd grader.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The samples show a good variety of question types, including straightforward definitions ('What figure has two endpoints and a definite length?'), model recognition ('Look at the diagram of a triangle. Each of its straight sides with two endpoints is an example of a ___.'), and procedural drawing questions ('When drawing a line, what symbols are placed at both ends').

competency_alignment.rationale: The items are strictly aligned to the MATATAG curriculum text. There is no scope creep into naming specific rays or lines with complex notation, or measuring angles. The focus remains tightly on 'Recognize, using models, and draws a point, line, line segment, and ray.'

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The numerical values and spatial concepts used are appropriate. Using '4 cm' in 'To draw a line segment measuring 4 cm, you start at the 0 cm mark on a ruler and draw until which mark?' is highly plausible and grounds the geometric concepts in basic, age-appropriate measurement.
